items.reason: Law-3 documented opt-out (suppressed as a finding, parked visibly). The L-21 guard is identity-based: only the base-constructor DefaultDispatchHook trips HookNotSet. A freshly deployed DefaultDispatchHook, or any non-accruing hook (e.g. a mint-debt hook with ratio 0), passes the guard and recreates L-21's zero-mint-debt outcome. Story-051 Concerns and NatSpec UniPoolerV2.sol:91-97 document this as a deliberate escape hatch; test_hookGuard_freshDefaultDispatchHook_isDeliberateBypass pins it. No phStaging2 script constructs a DefaultDispatchHook (grep, excl. lib/test). A stale mint-debt hook still bound to BalancerPoolerV2 fails LOUDLY (OnlyDispatcher). Code-scan judges it not a footgun (a competent owner would not be surprised that a no-op hook accrues no debt). Pattern-matcher rated it a residual Law-3 footgun at low confidence. Human decides at /ledger; does NOT block proposing L-21 fixed.

pattern.description: The L-21 fix guard `if (address(hook) == _defaultHook) revert HookNotSet()` (L356; _defaultHook captured at L230) blocks only the one DefaultDispatchHook instance deployed by the base constructor. A different no-op hook (for example a second DefaultDispatchHook, or a stale hook redeployed by a script) passes the guard and recreates the L-21 zero-mint-debt outcome. setHook rejects only address(0) (ATokenDispatcherV2 L95). A mint-debt hook whose `dispatcher` is not repointed to UniPoolerV2 fails loudly in onDispatch (dispatcher-gated), which is safe. Reaching the bypass needs an owner/script action, so this is a residual Law-3 footgun, not an attacker path. The fix covers the failure mode L-21 states (setHook skipped or reordered).

econ.description: Until setHook, every index-4 NFTMinterV2.mint reverts UniPoolerV2__HookNotSet. The revert is atomic. Payment transferFrom and price growth roll back, and no PSM donation, sUSDS wrap or nudge collection happens, so no price, rate or debt state changes. Knock-on effect: BatchNFTMinter.batchMint (phoenix-nft-staking BatchNFTMinter.sol:238-290) loops nftMinter.mint(dispatcherIndex, …). If its dispatcherIndex is 4, the usual configuration since UniPoolerV2 donates to batchMinter, the whole batch reverts as well. Meanwhile the NudgeStreamer keeps releasing nudge that was already collected into the batchMinter's deliverable pot. Nothing new enters, because donations need mints. The first batchMint after setHook collects the pot that built up during the window. This is the nudge's normal incentive behaviour after any pause or quiet period, and it is capped by nudge already streamed. Compared with the pre-fix behaviour (L-21: mints succeed while accruing zero phUSD mint-debt, an unbacked-mint leak), this is strictly better.
econ.economicImpact: Liveness only, for the cutover window between replaceDispatcher(4) and setHook (plan Stage 2 steps 5→6). No value is lost or mispriced. The accumulated nudge pot goes to the first post-window batch minter, the same as after any quiet period.
econ.attackScenario: None adversarial. The window is owner-controlled.
econ.profitability: n/a. A searcher could race the first post-setHook batchMint for the accumulated pot. That is the nudge's designed incentive, not a leak.
econ.affectedParties: Index-4 minters and batch minters, who are delayed during the window.
econ.relatedLedger: L-21 6867d791 (FIX-COMPLETE per code-scan). Run-21 code-scan setAside MR-002 already covers the ordering.
econ.recommendation: Run replaceDispatcher(4), hook.setDispatcher(UniPoolerV2) and UniPoolerV2.setHook(hook) in one multisig batch so the window is zero blocks.
econ.confidence: medium (BatchNFTMinter.dispatcherIndex == 4 is on-chain config, not verified here)

items.reason: Law-3 trusted residual of the Q-19 fix: the canonical check derives its factory from the caller-supplied router_, so a wrong router plus a matching fake factory would pass. Router and pair are deploy-time owner inputs (obvious misconfig, not a footgun) unless the deploy script reads router_ from an unverified source. Supports proposing Q-19 fixed; recorded so the trust root is visible. The 'pair must exist pre-deploy' half is MR21-02/LC-21-02.

verbatim.description: The canonical check takes its factory from the caller-supplied router_ (IUniswapV2Router02(router_).factory()). A wrong router plus a matching fake factory would pass. Router and pair are both deploy-time owner/deployer inputs, so this is Law-3 trusted (an obvious misconfig) unless the deploy script reads the router from an unverified source. The check also needs the pair to exist before deployment (getPair returns 0 and pair_ != 0), which pushes pair creation and seeding into the L-24 pre-seed window.

items.reason: Ledger-suppressed against owner wont-fix L-22/L-23 (same root cause, no higher ceiling), but parked here for recall: L-23's triageReason ('lightning strike', accidental same-block staleness at mint cadence) does not address an attacker DELIBERATELY poisoning the keeper's quote (swap lever pre-existing; donation lever new in 267660b via sync()/balanceOf quotePool, dominated by the swap lever). L-22's tolerance rationale bounds extraction at the keeper tolerance either way, but neither triageReason says it covers the deliberate case. Human: confirm L-22/L-23 cover deliberate poisoning (no re-file proposed) or reopen.

priorWontFixDisclosure.L-22: Owner triage 2026-10-01: intended by design. Owner: "That's the nature of tolerance. We're literally tolerating an attack of this size." The keeper-chosen tolerance t is the accepted MEV budget; per-zap extraction is bounded at ~0.44*t*Delta (ECON-001) on protocol-owned liquidity only, no user funds. Disposition does NOT cover sibling L-06 (342075dfba, BalancerPoolerV2.pool), which stays open, nor L-23 (shared-venue floor staleness), whose stale-floor mechanism could widen the effective tolerance beyond t.
priorWontFixDisclosure.L-23: Owner triage 2026-10-01: wont-fix. Owner: "The frequency of NFT minting is not live trading. This scenario is a lightning strike rather than a common inconvenience." Basis: the coupling only bites when UniPoolerV2.pool and PromotionUniV2_Eth Leg A land in the same block on stale quotes; at NFT-mint cadence that collision is rare, and extraction stays tolerance-bounded and POL-only (same tier as L-15 e64f73d629, L-06 342075dfba, L-22 ycn20l22, all wont-fix). Operational guidance retained: do not batch both calls in one block; quote the second after the first is mined. Revisit if dispatch cadence rises toward continuous/keeper-batched trading.

items.operationalGuidance: Operational only. The keeper should check that pair.balanceOf equals getReserves() when it quotes (no pending donation), and should bound its floors against an off-chain reference such as PhusdStableMinter's $1 mint price, not spot alone. No code change.
items.confidence: high (root cause); rationale coverage is the open question

items.reason: Ledger-suppressed against owner wont-fix L-24 (not widened: sync() was always permissionless; quotePool returns expectedLP=0 on ts==0 so a quote-driven keeper refuses). Recorded for recall because pool() now syncs first, so a dust-donated empty canonical pair becomes poolable at the donor ratio if a keeper hand-sets minLP>0. Cutover runbook (phStaging2:100/101/103/108) should create-and-seed atomically and derive floors from quotePool only.

priorWontFixDisclosure.L-24: Owner triage 2026-10-01: wont-fix. Owner: "This is a mild inconvenience at most." Basis: a third-party dust pre-seed only trips the cutover's fail-loud reserves==(0,0) precondition, so the impact is delay on a one-off cutover; the griefer gains nothing and the skew is cheaply and profitably arbitraged back. Safe-recovery guidance retained (footgun): if the pair is pre-seeded, arbitrage it to the target ratio, then seed via direct transfer + pair.mint with a reserve-ratio assertion. Never relax the precondition or router-addLiquidity with zero mins into a skewed pair. Does not cover Q-19 ycn20q19 (pair not bound to router factory), which is triaged separately.

items.operationalGuidance: No code change. The cutover runbook (phStaging2:108) should seed the pair in the same transaction as, or before, any pool() call, and keepers should derive floors from quotePool only (a 0 expectedLP refuses to pool, which is the safe behaviour). Faithfulness note: the protocol can create-and-seed atomically via Router02.addLiquidity before deploying UniPoolerV2 (constructor accepts a seeded pair), closing the empty-canonical-pair window.
